lessons: CRITICAL fixed, and this is the headline of the cycle: the skill said Bank of Israel 'does not legally cap PTI, but flags >40% as high risk'. BOTH halves were wrong. Directive 329 section 5 is a HARD PROHIBITION at 50% ('תאגיד בנקאי לא יאשר ולא יבצע הלוואה לדיור, בשיעור החזר מהכנסה העולה על 50%'), and the 40% figure in section 6 is a BANK CAPITAL rule (100% risk weight), not a borrower cap and not a mere flag. Now encoded as a ceiling on the bank plus a cost cliff, with an explicit warning never to tell a user they may borrow up to 50% PTI.

REVOKED, do NOT re-seed: the v1.2.1 cycle recorded 'PTI over 40% high-risk flag with a Prime+3 stress test' under 'Confirmed-correct-do-not-relitigate'. That line is how the defect survived. It was never verified against the directive text; it was carried forward on the strength of an earlier cycle's assertion. Treat every 'confirmed, do not relitigate' entry in this file as a hypothesis until re-read at the primary source.

CRITICAL fixed (fabrication): 'Israeli mortgages must contain at least two tracks by Bank of Israel regulation' was invented. The word מסלול does not appear in Directive 329 at all, and the directive sets no minimum track count. Removed, and inverted into a Gotcha so an agent does not re-derive it.

CRITICAL fixed (fabrication): 'Banks must run a stress test assuming Prime + 3 percentage points' was attributed to BoI regulation. Directive 329 contains no stress-test requirement (zero hits for תרחיש / עמידות / מבחן). Recast as prudent borrower practice, explicitly labelled as advice and not regulation.

CRITICAL fixed: the prime-specific cap question is settled at source. The word פריים does not appear anywhere in Directive 329. There is no Prime-specific cap in force; the only composition limit is section 7's 66.66% on the WHOLE variable-rate portion. Note the skill previously wrote the complement as 33.33%, which is arithmetically wrong against a 66.66% cap; it is 33.34%. The claim is now stated as what the current text contains, NOT as 'the prime cap was scrapped in year X', because no source for that date was fetched this cycle.

MAJOR fixed (found only by fetching): the gov.il page cited as a 'multi-track payment calculator that accounts for CPI linkage' is nothing of the sort. Its title is 'מחשבון לחישוב ניקוד וגובה ההלוואה לדיור (משכנתא)', an eligibility-POINTS calculator for the government assistance loan. Both the Reference Links row and the Troubleshooting instruction that sent users there to model CPI have been corrected. A URL returning 200 says a page exists, not that it is the page you described.

MAJOR fixed: the 'Foreign-resident max LTV 50% (regulatory ceiling)' row was unsourced. Directive 329 section 2 classifies by PROPERTY (single / replacement / investment), not by residency, and has no foreign-resident row. Residency appears only in section 12.3, which exempts FX and FX-linked loans to a foreign resident from the section-7 variable cap. Row removed and replaced with a classification instruction.

Fixed (surfaced by the Judge): the reservist mortgage-protection section overclaimed. It tied the deferral to a '5 or more consecutive days' Order-8 threshold and called the protections 'permanent'. Verification: the 5-consecutive-days threshold actually belongs to a separate right (a spouse's daily work-absence entitlement), and the reservist payment-deferral (commonly up to ~3 months, no interest/fees) is set largely by the active-period relief framework, not a blanket permanent statute. Reworded to a verify-before-quoting framing and added an evidence entry (Kol-Zchut reservist Q&A).

Confirmed-correct-do-not-relitigate (2026, verified): LTV ceilings 75/70/50 (foreign 50) under Directive 329; the at-least-one-third-fixed track-composition rule (old Prime<=1/3 cap removed, Directive 329 update published 27.12.2020); purchase-tax brackets (single-apt 0% bracket ceiling, investment 8%/10% brackets) frozen through 2027 (next update 15.1.2028); PTI over 40% high-risk flag with a Prime+3 stress test; and the Iron Swords / wartime BoI mortgage-relief framework being an activatable, time-boxed measure (reservist Order-8 protections permanent). The mortgage-monthly-payment checker takes the interest rate as a USER INPUT with generic defaults, so a BoI rate change does not affect it (re-verify only, no rebuild).

CRITICAL fixed: the BoI rate in the Snapshot was stale (it lagged a cut). Snapshot updated to the then-current BoI rate and its derived Prime; the BoI rate is the single most drift-prone figure here and must be re-checked on every use.

A temporary BoI relief framework is active again in 2026 during conflict periods. Replaced the absolute claim with verify-at-boi.org.il-before-quoting language; the statutory reservist (Order 8) protections are permanent and stated as such.
